# Fermi-Sea Preparation Time

Question: how long must an autonomous, translation-invariant fermionic reservoir with strictly finite-range jumps take to prepare a critical Fermi sea at fixed whole-state fidelity?

Read science/paired_reservoirs.md for the main pairing-inclusive theorem, exact resource normalization, scalar Gram inequality, pair-parity witness, Taylor and root-deletion proof, and near-linear necessary radius for polynomial time. The translation-invariant quadratic Hamiltonian is unrestricted in range and strength.
Read science/model.md for the separate gain/loss class, its per-mode cap and exact all-input occupation dynamics.
Read science/root_budget.md and science/time_converse.md for the narrower explicit finite-size weighted-root and Jensen estimates.
Read science/construction.md for the inherited geometric-root filters, sufficient time and coefficient precision.
Read science/interpretation.md and science/limitations.md for the operational scope and companion result.
Read references/RELATED_WORK.md for primary sources and attribution.
Read verification/README.md and verification/run_all.py for numerical checks, including mixed linear jumps and strong pairing in two-mode Fock space.

For self-directed learning, use learning/README.md, learning/anchor_bridge.md and learning/milestones.md. The educational anchor is Breuer and Petruccione, The Theory of Open Quantum Systems (2002). The map retains M01–M30 and follows the narrow solvable setting into the paired theorem.
